data.reason: Genuine: final-core/final-full ship no USER and the CLI passes --user only on Linux (internal/engineclient/client.go sets cfg.User under runtime.GOOS==linux), so on Windows/macOS hosts the engine runs as root - verified live, this dogfood container's Config.User is empty. Dockerfile already pre-creates 0777 /reports,/scan and HOME=/tmp for arbitrary uids, so baking a nonroot USER into the finals is compatible defense-in-depth.

CVE-2019-20477 (PyYAML 5.1, CVSS 9.8, fixed 5.2) is real but pinned only in internal/finding/testdata/fixture/requirements.txt - a deliberately vulnerable fixture planted to exercise the finding pipeline; scripts/smoke.ps1 copies it into a throwaway temp repo and never installs it. Build/test-only test data with no runtime path in cavet (a Go module; no Python runtime).

SERVICE_API_KEY in the finding-pipeline fixture is synthetic by construction: the file's own comments document it as 'Not a real credential... deliberately not shaped like any provider's token' so gitleaks' generic-api-key rule fires on staged content during tests. The detection is the fixture's purpose, not a leak; the AWS pair above it is AWS's canonical documentation example, allowlisted by GitHub and gitleaks.

Smoke-test marker key: lines 32-33 of scripts/smoke.ps1 define $SmokeKey as a deliberately high-entropy value 'shaped so gitleaks generic-api-key rule flags the staged content'; it is written only into a throwaway temp repo to assert scan --staged exits 1, then the repo is deleted. Not a credential.

The flagged 0o755 at internal/cli/hook.go:15 is os.MkdirAll on the .cavet/hooks DIRECTORY: directories need the execute bit for traversal, and the pre-commit/pre-commit.cmd shims written beneath it (lines 19, 25) must be 0o755 for git to invoke them via core.hooksPath. 0600 applies to secret-bearing files, not an executable hook directory; no secrets are written here.

data.question: 47 of the 64 baseline rows on cavet's own repo come from internal/finding/testdata/fixture/** (26 CVE rows from requirements.txt, 16+1 terraform, 4 python/secrets) - findings the project deliberately planted to exercise the pipeline. Every fresh clone re-baselines them as debt, so the one genuine signal in the table (engine container runs as root on non-Linux hosts, 856924 confirmed) drowns in self-inflicted noise. How should cavet treat its own fixtures: config-level path excludes, inline per-fixture dismissals committed to the log, or a testdata-aware default in init/scan?
